entries.title: How soccer brings a Bhutanese community together in Harrisburg, Pa.

entries.snippet: U.S. Housing Secretary Scott Turner said Monday that nine years after the territory received $1.9 billion in disaster recovery funding, it has spent less than a third of the funds.

entries.snippet: The move, announced Monday, could unleash a new wave of economic chaos, with risks of higher inflation and further fraying of relations between two nations that had been closely woven together before Trump's return to the White House.

entries.title: The highlights and controversies of the 2026 World Cup
entries.snippet: There was a hero's welcome for the Spanish soccer team as they arrived in Madrid, where throngs of fans cheered their triumphant World Cup win. Spain's victory ended Argentina and its star Lionel Messi's reign, and caps off a tournament that defied expectations on several fronts.

entries.title: Remembering PBS programming executive Sylvia Bugg
entries.snippet: The PBS family is mourning the passing of one of its own, Sylvia Bugg. Sylvia most recently served as chief programming executive and general manager for general audience programming. She was a dedicated and passionate leader, and a staunch supporter of our team at the News Hour.

entries.title: A wave of student loan borrowers have entered default since pandemic-era protections lapsed
entries.snippet: Today, around 9.5 million people — 1 in 5 federal student loan borrowers — are in default, meaning they are more than nine months behind on their payments.

entries.title: FDA is still focused on lettuce supplier as source of parasite, despite faulty test result
entries.snippet: Federal health officials said Monday they remain focused on lettuce from Taylor Farms as the source of a multistate outbreak of a diarrhea-causing parasite, despite inaccurate test results that the government briefly publicized over the weekend.

entries.title: British prosecutors charge a man with murder in death of former politician Ann Widdecombe
entries.snippet: Joshua Kerry was charged after more than a week in custody on suspicion of murder and acts of terror.

entries.title: 5 dead after group attempted to save a struggling swimmer in an Ohio river
entries.snippet: The tragedy occurred two days after five members of a family were killed in southern Utah after a flash flood swept through canyons during a hiking trip.

entries.snippet: The entrance of Darline Graham into the Republican scramble to select a new Senate nominee further complicates an already rushed process following Lindsey Graham's death earlier this month.

entries.title: Tropical Storm Bertha forms along U.S. Gulf Coast
entries.snippet: Tropical Storm Bertha has formed in the Gulf of Mexico and is expected. Bertha is the second named storm of the Atlantic hurricane season.

entries.title: Italy: Protests in Bologna over death of immigrant in police custody
entries.snippet: Demonstrators are demanding answers over the death of 42-year-old Abderrahim Fakir. Local authorities have urged calm while the investigation is underway.

entries.title: Why the youth jobs crisis is becoming global
entries.snippet: Young people in much of the world face growing competition for entry-level jobs as graduate numbers rise, hiring slows and AI-driven disruption adds uncertainty to career prospects.

entries.title: China, Philippines clash in South China Sea ahead of ASEAN meeting
entries.snippet: China and the Philippines traded accusations after a violent altercation between navy personnel in the disputed South China Sea. The incident heightened tensions ahead of a major diplomatic summit in Manila.

entries.title: Afghanistan: Deadly flash floods hit Nuristan province
entries.snippet: Some 20 people have been killed and more than 80 injured, with the city of Parun hit particularly hard. A lack of infrastructure and the effects of climate change have left the country vulnerable to natural disaster.

entries.title: How heat waves are messing with your sleep
entries.snippet: Residents across Europe have struggled to sleep during the latest record heat waves. But as the planet continues to warm, sleep deprivation could create an epidemic of mental and physical ill-health.

entries.title: Germany news: Merz hosts Azerbaijan President Aliyev
entries.snippet: Talks between the German chancellor and Ilham Aliyev have focused on energy. Meanwhile, Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt will present a report on sexual offenses against children. DW has more.

entries.title: India: Modi addresses exam leaks which sparked CJP protest
entries.snippet: India's prime minister has stressed that action was taken to hold those responsible for the leaks accountable. Opposition leader Gandhi has meanwhile called on Modi to step down. Follow DW.

entries.title: Tate brothers to fight extradition to UK, says lawyer
entries.snippet: Andrew and Tristan Tate's lawyer said that the brothers are victims of a "political witch hunt." He has vowed to challenge their extradition to the UK.

entries.title: UK's new PM Andy Burnham cuts household electricity tax
entries.snippet: The UK's new leader moved to remove VAT from electricity bills from October 1. The move comes before Burnham chairs his first cabinet meeting later today.

entries.title: US imposes new 50% tariff on many Canadian goods
entries.snippet: The tariffs will cover products including wine and hockey sticks, but not energy or fish. The move is the latest trade escalation between the US and its northern neighbor under the Trump administration.

entries.title: Iran war: US launches fresh strikes as Trump vows revenge
entries.snippet: The US has launched strikes on Iran for a 10th consecutive night as both sides vie for control of the Strait of Hormuz. US President Trump has promised revenge over the deaths of fallen American troops. DW has more.

entries.title: Mexican drug lord 'El Mayo' sentenced to life without parole in US prison
entries.snippet: Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada, a co-founder of the Sinaloa cartel and one of the world's most notorious drug traffickers, was sentenced to life in a US prison.

entries.title: AliExpress hit with record EU fine
entries.snippet: The Chinese retailer has become the latest major online marketplace to face penalties under the EU’s Digital Services Act.

entries.title: England and Liverpool football legend Kevin Keegan dies aged 75
entries.snippet: English former striker and manager Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75 after a battle with cancer. He was a two-time European footballer of the year with Hamburg.

entries.title: Russia says bus strike kills 5 in border region with Ukraine
entries.snippet: The strike comes as Ukraine launched more than hundreds of drones at Moscow after a Russian missile barrage on Kyiv, as President Zelenskyy sought to calm growing tensions over Ukraine’s military leadership.

entries.title: Guterres to visit Cyprus as UN seeks to revive peace talks
entries.snippet: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres will visit Cyprus next week in what is seen as an effort to kickstart the stalled peace process. Why now? What is known about the plan? And what might be different this time round?

entries.title: Why a 90-year-old treaty limits NATO in the Black Sea
entries.snippet: A 90-year-old treaty still shapes the balance of power in the Black Sea. As Ukraine fights on against Russia, can NATO project power into waters it can't enter freely?

entries.title: US ties to Israel rattle rare earth deal in Malaysia
entries.snippet: Malaysia's rare earth refinery in Gebeng is essential to a strategic deal between the Pentagon and Australia's Lynas mining corporation. Now, Malaysian activists are using it as leverage to support Palestinians in Gaza.

entries.title: Spain won the World Cup, but Donald Trump 'cast a shadow'
entries.snippet: Though Donald Trump mostly stayed clear of stadiums, the World Cup may influence the US midterm elections. DW looks at the political implications of "the most successful sporting event maybe in the history of the world."
